Biomarker‐based screening enables early detection of AL amyloidosis in intermediate/high‐risk MGUS patients. Our study shows that identifying pre‐symptomatic AL through biomarker longitudinal monitoring allows early treatment, leading to significant organ function recovery. To the Editor, Monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) is a widespread condition, often incidentally identified, with a risk of evolution in multiple myeloma (MM) or, although more rarely, in plasma cell‐related disorders including immunoglobulin light chain (AL) amyloidosis [ 1 ]. The outcome of AL amyloidosis is highly impacted by the extent of organ damage, in particular by cardiac involvement. Since the presenting symptoms of organ damage are highly heterogeneous and generally late, establishing an early diagnosis of AL amyloidosis can often be challenging. Nonetheless, late diagnosis, when organ involvement is advanced and the possibility of delivering effective therapy is limited, has a relevant impact on outcome [ 2 ]. Alteration of free light chain ratio (FLCr), a known risk factor for MGUS progression to MM, precedes the onset of AL amyloidosis by 4 years or more, thus offering a potential window for early diagnosis and treatment [ 3 ]. Alterations of biomarkers of organ dysfunction and damage, in particular N‐terminal‐pro‐natriuretic peptide type‐B (NT‐proBNP) for the heart, 24‐h proteinuria, predominantly albumin, for the kidney, and alkaline phosphatase (ALP) for the liver, can raise suspicion of initial pre‐symptomatic amyloid organ involvement in patients with MGUS. Implementing their use during the follow‐up in MGUS cases with abnormal FLCr could allow early identification of patients who deserve further diagnostic workup for AL amyloidosis [ 2 , 4 ]. Given these premises, biomarker‐based screening for AL amyloidosis has been systematically integrated since 2012 in the follow‐up of MGUS with alteration of FLCr to explore their role for early capturing pre‐symptomatic AL amyloidosis cases [ 2 ].

extracted_data.document_summary: This study investigates the feasibility and effectiveness of biomarker-based screening for the early detection of AL amyloidosis in intermediate/high-risk MGUS patients. It demonstrates that longitudinal monitoring, particularly in a cohort of 4742 MGUS patients with altered FLCr, significantly increases the timely identification of pre-symptomatic AL amyloidosis, leading to earlier treatment, limited organ involvement, and significant recovery of organ function.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-based longitudinal screening and monitoring strategy for AL amyloidosis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Systematically integrated since 2012 in a single-center longitudinal cohort of 4742 MGUS patients, with a median follow-up of 4 years. Specifically, 1375 patients (28.9%) with altered FLCr underwent sequential biomarker monitoring. No specific therapeutic doses or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focuses on a diagnostic screening strategy rather than a therapeutic intervention.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Alteration was observed in 1375 patients (28.9%) and precedes the onset of AL amyloidosis by 4 years or more; no specific reference range or normal limits provided.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Indicates clonal plasma cell activity and is a crucial risk factor for progression from MGUS to multiple myeloma or AL amyloidosis.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Longitudinal screening and monitoring of Monoclonal Gammopathy of Undetermined Significance (MGUS) patients for progression to AL amyloidosis.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Offers a critical window for early diagnosis and treatment of AL amyloidosis; its alteration triggers sequential biomarker monitoring and is a key indicator for potential progression, as no MGUS cases without FLCr alterations progressed to AL amyloidosis.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Detected in 9 out of 22 (40.9%) pre-symptomatic AL amyloidosis patients and 16 out of 38 (42.1%) MGUS cases without AL. Among those with cardiac involvement, one had a mild elevation (556 ng/L), with others at least 650 ng/L, indicating initial pre-symptomatic organ involvement.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Released in response to cardiac wall stress and volume overload, serving as a marker for cardiac dysfunction.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Biomarker-based longitudinal screening for pre-symptomatic AL amyloidosis cardiac involvement or other cardiac pathologies in MGUS patients.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates potential cardiac involvement in AL amyloidosis, suggesting the need for further diagnostic workup. While useful, it may be suboptimal for detecting early ATTRwt heart involvement; in non-AL cases, it indicated other cardiac conditions like hypertensive cardiomyopathy or arrhythmias.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Detected in 12 out of 22 (54.5%) pre-symptomatic AL amyloidosis patients and 20 out of 38 (52.6%) MGUS cases without AL, raising suspicion of initial pre-symptomatic organ involvement.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Indicates kidney damage or dysfunction, particularly compromise of the glomerular filtration barrier leading to protein leakage.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Biomarker-based longitudinal screening for pre-symptomatic AL amyloidosis renal involvement or other renal pathologies in MGUS patients.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of potential renal involvement in AL amyloidosis, suggesting the need for further diagnostic workup. In cases where AL was ruled out, it indicated other kidney diseases such as diabetic nephropathy or hypertensive nephrosclerosis.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Detected in 1 out of 22 (4.5%) pre-symptomatic AL amyloidosis patients with liver involvement and in 2 out of 38 (5.3%) MGUS cases without AL, raising suspicion of initial pre-symptomatic organ involvement.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: An enzyme found in the liver, bone, kidney, and digestive tract; elevated levels can indicate liver or bone disease, acting as a marker of liver dysfunction and damage.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Biomarker-based longitudinal screening for pre-symptomatic AL amyloidosis liver involvement or other liver pathologies in MGUS patients.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of potential liver involvement in AL amyloidosis, suggesting the need for further diagnostic workup. In cases where AL was ruled out, it indicated conditions such as non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.
